subject: POC KPI orchestration & next steps — Veridian AI trial
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Li <alex@veridian.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: POC KPI orchestration & next steps — Veridian AI trial

Alexandra — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth for the trial scope: 

Summary of ask: Veridian wants a 4–6 week trial to validate an LLM-powered response assistant for customer support workflows (30–60M sessions/month projected). Key risk areas are latency under load, per-token cost, and quality on sensitive support prompts.

Proposed high-level success criteria (please confirm or adjust):
- Latency: p95 inference latency <= 150 ms (end-to-end token generation for avg 128-token responses)
- Throughput: baseline 50 QPS sustained with burst to 150 QPS for 30s windows (95th percentile of observed load patterns)
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0005 (measured after batching/quantization)
- Quality: > 92% pass rate on Veridian’s golden prompt set (1000 labeled prompts; rubric: correctness + safety)
- Observability: request-level logging, per-route latency/cost breakdown, and model-version tagging enabled

Trial plan (high level):
1) Week 0 (onboarding): dataset upload + shared golden set + config of routes and rate limits
2) Week 1–2 (smoke & baseline): smoke tests, initial baseline runs at target latencies and small scale
3) Week 3–4 (scale & stress): ramp to target throughput; measure p95 and cost/token under representative traffic
4) Week 5–6 (readout): joint readout, pass/fail decision against KPIs, and handoff for production integration

Owners: Redwood will own runtime configuration, baseline performance runs, and instrumentation. Veridian will own golden set labeling and success rubric sign-off. I’ve copied Monica and Ben to align on ownership.

Deliverables I’ll attach: a working KPI spreadsheet (POC-success-metrics.xlsx) and a trial-onboarding checklist. Please flag any legal/security requirements we should route to the Private deployment path.

Next actions: 
- Alexandra: confirm KPI numbers above and whether the golden set is ready by Nov 20
- Nikhil/Redwood: prepare baseline test harness and share calendar slots for a 30–60 minute trial kickoff

Thanks —
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: POC-success-metrics.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: trial-onboarding-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alexandra Li <alex@veridian.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@veridian.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC KPI orchestration & next steps — Veridian AI trial

Nikhil — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Product and Security: 

1) KPIs
- Latency: Product would prefer p95 <= 120 ms if achievable, but we can accept <= 150 ms as the pass criterion for the trial; we will mark 120 ms as a stretch goal.
- Throughput: 50 QPS baseline is fine; can you confirm expected GPU footprint for that baseline?
- Cost: target cost/token is tight; Tom in Legal/Security asked us to capture both cost/token and projected monthly spend at expected volume.
- Quality: we will deliver a 1k golden set by Nov 20. Our rubric will include a safety flag column (yes/no).

2) Data/security
- We need an NDA scoping note for logs retention — Tom will send a short template. For the trial we require logs to be stored in a customer-controlled bucket or masked before leaving our environment.

3) Timeline
- 6-week timeline is acceptable; we prefer kickoff the week of Nov 23 (team availability).

Accepting the plan aside from the security/log retention detail. Tom, I’ve looped you in for the retention/NDA items. Thanks —
Alexandra
Head of Product, Veridian AI

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC KPI orchestration & next steps — Veridian AI trial

Nikhil / Ben — following Alex’s reply I put together a concrete evaluation plan and owner map so we can move quickly once golden set and retention requirements are confirmed. See below (this will go into the shared runbook).

Evaluation plan (detailed):
- Data ingestion (owner: Ben Carter): validate golden set schema (fields: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_answer, safety_flag). Run a quick schema conformance job within 24h of receipt.
- Baseline harness (owner: Nikhil Sharma): create a reproducible harness that runs 1000 sample prompts at controlled concurrency to capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens-per-response. Harness code and docker image will be in the REDWOOD-TRIAL repo.
- Costing (owner: Ben Carter): run token-level costing with three configurations: default FP16, int8 quantized, and batching=dynamic. Produce a per-config cost/token and projected monthly spend table.
- Quality measurement (owner: Veridian / Alexandra): apply rubric to golden set; we'll store results in a shared spreadsheet with pass/fail + comments.
- Observability & retention (owner: Nikhil + Security): implement request-level IDs, per-route tagging, and a retention policy. We will propose two options: (A) logs masked and forwarded to Veridian bucket, (B) logs remain in Redwood for 14 days with masked PII; choose A for production parity.

Acceptance gates (to mark as "ready for readout"):
1) Golden set uploaded and validated
2) Baseline harness run completed with p95 measurement and cost table produced
3) Observability endpoints and minimal alerting configured (p95 spike alert and error rate > 1% alert)

Timeline (owner-driven milestones):
- Nov 20: Golden set delivery (Veridian)
- Nov 23–27: Kickoff + onboarding (Redwood + Veridian)
- Nov 30–Dec 4: Baseline runs and early quality measurement
- Dec 7–11: Scale runs and cost modeling
- Dec 14: Joint readout and pass/fail decision
I’ll draft the runbook by EOD today and share the link to the trial repo. Ben — please prepare the costing sheet template (I left a placeholder tab in the attached POC-success-metrics.xlsx).

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-17T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC KPI orchestration & next steps — Veridian AI trial

Alex / Tom — great, thanks for the confirmations. Quick notes and final next steps before kickoff: 

- We can target p95 <= 120 ms as a stretch; for the baseline we’ll measure against 150 ms as the official pass threshold. If we achieve <120 ms on baseline hardware we’ll flag as "exceeded" in the readout.
- GPU footprint: For 50 QPS baseline we expect to need 2x A100-40GB equivalents in Dedicated (or equivalent on hosted with autoscaling). I’ll include a short sizing note in the trial repo.
- Logs/retention: agreed — Tom, if you can send the retention template, we will propose option A (masked logs to your bucket) as first preference and include an HMAC of request IDs for verification.

Calendar: proposed kickoff slots next week — https://cal.redwood.ai/nikhil/30m (pick any slot and I’ll send a calendar invite).

Attachments again: POC-success-metrics.xlsx (filled-in draft tabs for baseline, cost models, and owner checklist), trial-onboarding-checklist.pdf.

I'll proceed to create the REDWOOD-TRIAL repo and drop the baseline harness scaffold once Alex confirms the kickoff slot.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
